title: Many Roots: Scion counts distinct courses, not repeated atoms

ciFast.note: Fast verification passed on the exact v0.16.10 main merge, including 4,336 passing tests, the strict 40-fixture main evaluation, build, and bundle budgets.

ciDeep.note: The local proof covers input-bound group derivation, explicit-label collision rejection, group-balanced packet selection, end-to-end group-hash integrity, offline reviewer export, and truthful incomplete-coverage reporting. No completed instructor review or trained adapter is claimed.

deploy.note: GitHub Pages built and deployed the exact verified v0.16.10 main merge.

liveProvider.note: This release tightens offline evidence identity and campaign readiness rather than changing hosted inference; public Scion remains the verified browser-local base-only route.

manualHuman.note: The corrected packet remains available for instructor review, but it contains only one distinct course group per current domain and zero completed judgments.

claims.summary: Every neutral candidate receives a stable readable course-group ID and SHA-256 bound to its exact canonical course input; same-input model variants share a group, while one explicit label reused across different inputs excludes every affected pair.

Blind packet sampling balances domain, course-group hash, and atom kind; protocol v3 binds the public case and reviewer JSON to a private organizer digest covering the exact source row and A/B mapping, and ingestion carries the verified group into approved corpus rows.

The current 309 candidates and 160 selected cases resolve to four course groups, exactly one per domain; the committed receipt reports those counts and remains reviewable but incomplete until every domain has at least three distinct groups and the domain target is met.

Course-group auditing reveals a smaller effective evidence base rather than promoting a model: completed instructor reviews remain zero, research training remains blocked, and public Scion stays on the pinned local Gemma base plus model-neutral compiler.
